items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: It’s the same I felt about Billie Holiday and even Fats Navarro

ctx.x: members of his race. Do you think that what he did had social implications or was it more just his musical prowess?

I never thought it had social implications. I just thought he was Bird and he was a genius. And I always felt like he was in transient here. It’s the same I felt about Billie Holiday and even Fats Navarro and some of the great players that left us so early. But in Bird’s case, I really always felt that he was like a bird. He flew here, he blew those notes, he showed us that music and then he took off again. I thought he was just here to show us the way. I never found it was social. I don’t know, maybe it was, but…
How did he feel about being – as you said — a God? Was he confident about his own abilities?
